title: Are You Alice?
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A disillusioned young man who has thrown away his dreams wanders into Wonderland and is named the 89th 'Alice', a role that obliges him to take part in a game to kill the White Rabbit under the Queen of Hearts' rules. Players who fail become 'Regrets', lost souls chasing a role.
life_message: It suggests that a person must face their past and find their own purpose rather than live out a script others impose.

content.note: Gun-carrying protagonist in a death game to kill the White Rabbit; murders and child deaths (MU Blood and Gore, Murder/s, Child/ren Death; AniList Death Game; review).
Dark, twisty psychological tone with hallucinations (review; MU Hallucination/s; AniList Psychological).
None noted in sources; MU lists Cross-dressing (to verify).
Protagonist described as a sarcastic 'teen punk'; coarse language likely (to verify).
Regret, resignation and a hidden past drive the story (review; MU Regret, Hidden Past).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are settled within the game's rules, but Alice relies on his own gun (Yen Press blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Alice rails against the role forced on him by the Queen's rules (Yen Press; review).

Civic vs kin.evidence: No family focus; bonds form among Wonderland characters (to verify).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: The Queen of Hearts' command is shown as oppressive (review).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: No religion; roles are literary scripts rather than faith (review).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: The search for personal identity and purpose is central (review).

folkways.japan: A Japanese reworking of Lewis Carroll common in josei and otome-style media, with bishonen versions of Wonderland characters.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer calls it twisty and confusing, giving 'not enough answers in the beginning' (Fantasy-Faction).
delivery.note: Themes of identity and imposed roles are left for readers to infer from a puzzle-like plot.

winners_losers: Sympathy goes to Alice and those resisting their assigned roles; the Queen's rule of forbidden memory is cast as oppressive (to verify ending).
to_verify: The review covers early volumes only; the ending and who 'wins' are not confirmed.
